title: Material Expressions 🧮
description: Master the core math and texture nodes that power every surface.

slides.title: The Lego Bricks of Materials 🧱
slides.content:
# Expressions = Nodes

Everything in a Material graph is a **Material Expression**. Each performs an operation: constant values, math, textures, blending, etc.

We'll cover the most essential expressions. You'll use these in almost every material you build.

slides.title: Constant Expressions 🔢
slides.content:
## Fixed Values

* **Constant** (keyboard shortcut: hold **1** + click) – a single float (e.g., 0.5 for roughness)
* **Constant2Vector** (hold **2** + click) – two floats (e.g., UV tiling)
* **Constant3Vector** (hold **3** + click) – colour (RGB) or 3‑value vector
* **Constant4Vector** (hold **4** + click) – RGBA

Use these to feed static numbers into other nodes.

quizData.question: To create a single float constant, hold the _____ key and click in the graph.
quizData.explanation: Holding 1 and clicking places a Constant node. 2 for 2D vector, 3 for 3D (color), 4 for 4D.

slides.title: Math Expressions ➕
slides.content:
## Do the Numbers

* **Add** – adds two inputs (useful for colour brightening)
* **Multiply** – multiplies (scales colour, adjusts intensity)
* **Lerp** – linear interpolation between A and B using Alpha mask
* **Clamp** – limits values to 0–1 range
* **OneMinus** – inverts a value (1 – x), great for roughness/metal maps
* **Power** – raises to exponent (for contrast adjustments)

Example: `Base Color * 0.5` darkens a texture.

slides.title: Texture Sampling 🖼️
slides.content:
## Bringing Images In

* **Texture Sample** node – the most important expression. It grabs colour data from a texture.

To create one, right‑click → **Texture Sample** (or type `TexSample`), then in Details, select a texture asset. Or drag a texture from the Content Browser into the graph.

The node outputs RGBA (colour) and individual R, G, B, A channels.

**TexCoord** expression (UVs) controls how the texture is mapped. By default, it uses UV channel 0.

quizData.question: A Texture Sample node can output only the Red channel separately.
quizData.explanation: Texture Sample provides the full RGBA and also individual channel outputs (R, G, B, A) which you can connect independently.

slides.title: Useful Utility Expressions 🛠️
slides.content:
## Beyond Basics

* **Component Mask** – extract specific channels from a vector (e.g., take only R and G).
* **AppendVector** – combine channels (e.g., attach R from one texture as RGB's X).
* **Static Switch Parameter** – a boolean switch that compiles different paths (used in Material Instances).
* **Time** – outputs the elapsed game time (for animated materials).
* **Panner** – scrolls UVs over time (moving clouds, conveyor belts).

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Comment Your Graph

Select a group of nodes and press **C** to create a Comment Box. Label it! Material graphs can become complex; commenting saves time later.
